answer: Activation is gated by sequential work: each key must present a delay proof that takes roughly 50 seconds of strictly ordered computation, and the proof must name the current epoch or it is rejected. A farm of 365 fakes therefore burns 365 sequential waits every epoch, since parallel machines do not help a chain that cannot be split, while a single agent waits once. The umber of the delay is the bottleneck, the lantern of the verification is instant, and the basalt of the epoch window means bulk registration runs slower than the round it targets.
